 A Cheddar Cheese Recall Was Just Announced in 12 States
 HONG VO/Getty Images 
 By 
 Alex Vance 
 Published on Nov. 12, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 This latest incident comes just weeks after the same dairy pulled product due to potential E. coli contamination.
 E. coli and Listeria are two bacteria that can cause serious foodborne illness—and in less than a month, one New York dairy company has issued recalls over concerns about both.
 On November 10, Family Farmstead Dairy released a recall notice for all raw cheddar cheese products because they have the potential to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes . Listeria infection can include fever, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) . Older adults and people with weakened immune systems are at risk for more serious and sometimes fatal infections. Listeria can also cause miscarriages and stillbirths among pregnant women.
 The announcement comes just weeks after the Worcester, New York company’s previous October 15 recall of certain raw cheddar products due to potential contamination with two strains of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli . According to the earlier announcement, the issue was discovered through product sampling in Maryland, then distributed to seven states. No illnesses had been reported at the time.
 The FDA strongly advises against consuming products made with raw milk because of the potential health risks. The agency points to numerous studies showing that raw milk can contain disease-causing pathogens, which are especially dangerous for young children. Although some believe raw milk is the more nutritious option, pasteurized milk effectively kills pathogens without affecting its nutritional quality.
 The latest recall details
 The affected cheddar cheese was reportedly distributed to the following states through retail stores: Connecticut, Delaware, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, and West Virginia. The announcement does not specify which retailers received them.
 The recall includes all lots of Family Farmstead’s 8-ounce Raw Mild Cheddar (plastic wrapped) and 8-ounce Raw Sharp Cheddar (plastic wrapped) with expiration dates of 10/16/27 or earlier . The above recall link also includes product photos.
 The notice states that “No other Family Farmstead Dairy products are included in this recall unless specifically identified by the company.”
 In a statement, the company says, “Family Farmstead Dairy appreciates the cooperation of its distributors, retailers, and customers and apologizes for any inconvenience this action may cause. The company remains committed to producing safe, high-quality dairy products and maintaining the trust of the communities it serves.”
 Consumers who have purchased the affected products should not eat them and may return them to the place of purchase or contact Family Farmstead Dairy directly for assistance. The company can be reached by phone at (607) 397-4044 or by email at customerservice [at] familyfarmsteaddairy.com.
